changes.note: The class used to configure API request settings has been removed; configuration moves to ShopifyAPI::Context.setup.
The API request version was set by ShopifyAPI::Base.api_version; it is now the api_version configured in ShopifyAPI::Context.setup.
User-Agent was set by ShopifyAPI::Base.header; it is now the user_agent_prefix configured in ShopifyAPI::Context.setup. Other custom headers go on ShopifyAPI::Clients::HttpRequest.
Sessions can no longer be activated through ShopifyAPI::Base; use ShopifyAPI::Context.activate_session, or pass a session when instantiating a client.

The dependency on the graphql-client gem is deprecated. Existing queries and response parsing must be refactored onto the new GraphQL HTTP Client classes, and the schema no longer needs dumping to a local JSON file.

changes.before:
ShopifyAPI::Base.api_version = "2023-04"
client = ShopifyAPI::GraphQL.client
result = client.query(SHOP_NAME_QUERY)
shop_name = result.data.shop.name
changes.after:
client = ShopifyAPI::Clients::Graphql::Admin.new(session: session, api_version: "2023-04")
response = client.query(query: query)
shop_name = response.body["data"]["shop"]["name"]
changes.note: The guide's worked GraphQL refactor: the client is constructed with a session, and the response is a plain body hash rather than a parsed result object.
The use of ActiveResource is deprecated; REST requests must be refactored to the new format that better represents the REST API schema.
Finding many records moves from find(:all, params:) to a plain all(...) with keyword arguments.
Finding one record now takes id: as a keyword argument.

changes.before:
order = Order.find<id>
order.fulfillment_status = "fulfilled"
order.note = "Fulfilled on September 6, 2023"
order.save
changes.after:
order = Order.find(id: <id>)
order.fulfillment_status = "fulfilled"
order.note = "Fulfilled on September 6, 2023"
order.save!
changes.note: Saving is now the bang method. Quoted as the guide writes it, including its own `Order.find<id>` typo in the before column.
Generic post(:action) calls are replaced by named methods on a found record.
Deleting moves from an instance method to a class method taking id:.

Helper methods for related resource connections are gone; only properties listed in the REST API are supported. order.transactions is no longer supported because transactions is not a property of Order, while order.customer still is.
